item_taken.first_six_words: Household door: the unit is fixed
item_taken.why: The case's grain is fixed by the container the recorder is sent to, one visit per square and the card is what the door yields, and what moves when the container shrinks to the tetrad is the number of blanks and the number of errands, with the blanks that survive the visits, at the sea and on the private estate, being a class of miss and not a noise, which is Household door's tell; not Slip first, since the case never varies the attestation rule, a card is a card at both grains, only the container; not Rules before members, since the atlas counts returned cards, not rule-permitted positions; not Two-slot name, since the record keeps its two slots, species and cell, at both grains and the tetrad's added letter refines the cell's name rather than adding a slot; not One hand's move, since the errand is a visit paid per container, not an act that splits on 'and then'.

reasoning: The rule splits the case along one seam: the product of dimensions taken as the universe to count against, with its cell count as the denominator, goes to denominator-manufactures; what fixes one item stays here. The case states the square as 'a product of easting and northing cut at ten kilometres', states that the squares covering Britain and Ireland 'were the universe', states coverage as squares with a card over squares there are, and states that what moves with the grain is 'the cell count the fraction is taken against', the blanks, and the errands. Every one of those is the product-as-universe with its cell count as denominator, so the rule as written places the case on the target's side. What stays on this side is the one clause that fixes what an item is, 'a record is a species in a square', and it is not lost in crossing: the target names it as what the product makes countable. The rule does not say the case's facts change across, so none do.
case_out: A universe obtained by a product of dimensions: the Botanical Society of the British Isles' Atlas of the British Flora, 1962, Perring and Walters, took easting and northing, cut at ten kilometres, and their product, the 10-kilometre squares of the national grids, in Britain named by two letters and two digits, was the universe to count against, fixed by the scheme before any card was returned. The carrier is the product. What it makes countable: a record, a species in a square; a species' range, the number of squares with at least one record of it; and the scheme's own coverage, the number of squares with a card returned over the number of squares there are, a cardinal read off the grid and never visited to be counted. What it silently drops: where within a square a species was, since one record fills the square; and the squares at the sea and on the private estate stay in the denominator though no card can come back from them, so through the 1950s a square with no card was a blank that sent a recorder there, and the blanks that survived the visits were a fact about the recording and not about the flora. The tell that the denominator was manufactured rather than found: cut the same product at two kilometres, the tetrad, of which every 10-kilometre square holds exactly twenty-five, named by adding one letter to the square's name, the grain the later county floras recorded at, and a species recorded once in a 10-kilometre square fills that square and one tetrad of its twenty-five, so twenty-four cells stand blank at the finer cut that were full at the coarser, each a place to send someone; the denominator is twenty-five times larger and the coverage fraction falls without a single record changing; coarsen back to the 10-kilometre square and the twenty-four blanks close and the fraction rises. The records are the same pile at both cuts. What moves with the cut is the cell count the fraction is taken against, the number of blanks, and the number of errands.
